title: Six countries, one stove
excerpt: What I learned walking from Norway to Spain with a pack that weighed less than my cat.
content:
I left Bergen in May with a stove, a notebook and far too many socks.

Carry less

By Denmark I had posted home half of what I started with.

Eat well

A good dinner fixes almost any bad day on the trail.

Talk to people

The best routes were never in the guidebook. They came from farmers and bus drivers.

title: A night at the forest cabin
excerpt: Wood stove, bunk beds and a creek outside the door. How to book a Forest Service cabin, and why you should.
content:
There are over a hundred cabins you can rent in Montana's national forests, most for less than a motel.

Booking

They open six months ahead and the good ones go fast.

What's there

Bunks, a stove, an axe and an outhouse. Bring everything else.

Leave it better

Cut wood for the next people. They'll do the same for you.

title: June's one-pot trail chili
excerpt: The dinner our readers write to us about most. Twenty minutes, one pot, no washing up worth mentioning.
content:
This is the chili we cook on every cabin weekend.

At home

Mix the spices and dried beans in one bag, and the rice in another.

On the trail

Boil, add both bags, simmer for fifteen minutes.

To finish

A squeeze of lime and a handful of crushed tortilla chips.

title: The boots that lasted ten years
excerpt: Resoled twice, waxed every autumn, still going. A case for buying once and looking after it.
content:
My boots are older than Field Notes.

Buy repairable

Stitched soles can be replaced; glued ones usually can't.

Wax every autumn

Ten minutes a year keeps the leather alive.

Know when to stop

When the uppers crack, it's time. Mine haven't yet.

title: Hyalite in September
excerpt: Eleven waterfalls, one empty lake and the first snow on the peak. Notes from a weekday walk.
content:
We went on a Tuesday, the week after Labor Day.

The way up

The waterfalls were low but the willows had turned gold.

The lake

We had it to ourselves for an hour.

The way down

First snow on the peak behind us, and elk in the meadow.

title: Forty summers in a fire lookout
excerpt: Ruth has spent every summer since 1984 in a glass room on a mountain top. She told us what she's seen.
content:
Ruth climbs to her lookout every June and comes down in October.

The work

Watching for smoke, every day, all day, and calling it in.

The quiet

"People think it's lonely. It's the least lonely place I know."

The view

She has watched the same valley change for forty years.

title: Walking alone for the first time
excerpt: A reader's first solo walk, after our map and compass day. In her own words.
content:
I'd always walked with someone who knew the way.

Getting ready

I told two people my route and my time back.

On the trail

I checked the map more than I needed to. That was fine.

Coming home

I was back an hour early, and already planning the next one.
